description: The Highway-Runoff Database was developed by the US Geological Survey with the Federal Highway Administration to give planners and highway engineers planning-level information for assessing and mitigating the effects of highway runoff on receiving waters. This data release (version 1.0.0b) contains monitoring sites, precipitation, runoff and event-mean concentrations of water-quality constituents, compiled from 37 studies documented in 113 reports: data for 242 highway sites across the United States, 6,837 storm events from April 1975 to November 2017, and 106,441 concentration values for 414 constituents. It is packaged as a Microsoft Access application that calculates runoff-quality statistics with methods that handle censored concentrations. Coverage is national, at monitored sites. Access: a free USGS data release on ScienceBase (2018), with an associated USGS report. Caveats: the data span more than 40 years in which vehicle emissions and background sources changed, so early values reflect leaded petrol, phosphorus detergents and industrial deposition, and the Access format needs Windows software. It supports highway drainage design, environmental impact assessment of road runoff and stormwater interactions between road and water networks, and relates to the FHWA traffic records catalogued here.
